title: HB2985 (2026 Regular Session): Requires universal background checks for all sales or transfers of firearms

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official house.mo.gov or senate.mo.gov PDF of the version named in note (via LegiScan getBillText)

operative_text:
Section 571.201 (RSMo): 2. Any person who is not a licensed dealer, before transferring or attempting to transfer possession of a firearm, shall require that a background check be conducted on the prospective transferee and shall obtain approval of the transfer from the central repository after a background check. A person who is not a licensed dealer shall arrange for either a licensed dealer or law enforcement agency to obtain the background check.
Section 571.201 (RSMo): (3) A licensed dealer or law enforcement agency may charge a fee for conducting a background check, which shall not exceed twenty-five dollars or the cost of conducting the background check, whichever is greater.
Section 571.201 (RSMo): 4. (1) A prospective firearm transferee shall not accept possession of a firearm unless the prospective firearm transferor has obtained approval of the transfer from the central repository after a background check. (2) A prospective firearm transferee shall not knowingly provide false information to a prospective firearm transferor or to a licensed dealer for the purpose of acquiring a firearm.
Section 571.201 (RSMo): 5. If the central repository approves a transfer of a firearm in accordance with this section, the approval shall be valid for thirty calendar days, during which time the transferor and transferee may complete the transfer.
Section 571.201 (RSMo): 7. A violation of a provision of this section is a class B misdemeanor. Each day a violation of this section is committed or continued shall be considered a separate violation and punished accordingly.
Section 571.201 (RSMo): 8. In addition to any other penalty or remedy, the investigating law enforcement agency shall report any violation of this section committed by a licensed dealer to the attorney general, who shall report the violation to the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives within the United States Department of Justice.
